motion: Does evil and objective morality point to God, or can agnostic atheism explain moral experience without accepting a divine moral ground?

lockedRoutes.description: Infer a transcendent divine ground from objective moral facts and obligations, while challenging whether evolutionary naturalism can preserve their authority or the reliability of the reasoning used to deny them.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Establish that objective moral value is real, that it requires a transcendent personal ground, and that the proposed evolutionary account neither supplies normative authority nor defeats trust in that inference.

motionBridge.description: Objective evil and moral obligation make a divine moral ground the better explanation.

centralBridges.description: Moral experience tracks genuinely objective value rather than preference alone.
Objective moral value requires a transcendent standard grounded in God.
Undirected evolution cannot adequately secure confidence in truth-directed moral and rational beliefs.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Basic moral convictions are epistemically stronger than the skeptical premises offered against them.
Moral disagreement concerns knowledge or application and does not by itself defeat moral objectivity.

lockedRoutes.description: Explain moral experience as a human-centered evolutionary phenomenon organized around flourishing, while denying that experienced obligation establishes objective value or uniquely requires a divine ground.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that evolutionary and psychological mechanisms adequately explain moral experience, distinguish that explanatory burden from proving normative truth, and expose unsupported or circular steps from moral experience to God.

motionBridge.description: Agnostic atheism can explain moral experience without accepting a divine moral ground.

centralBridges.description: Evolutionary pressures and human psychology explain why moral judgments feel compelling.
Human-centered moral judgments do not remain objective independently of valuing subjects.
Moral experience does not uniquely establish God and may be explained without divine grounding.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Shared concern for flourishing permits practical moral reasoning from acknowledged assumptions.
Using divinely supplied reason to establish its divine source risks explanatory circularity.

lockedSections.title: Moral ontology and divine grounding
lockedSections.rationale: This section contains the principal inference from evil through objective goodness to God and the direct subjectivist challenge to that inference.

lockedSections.title: Moral phenomenology and evolution
lockedSections.rationale: This section tests whether deeply felt moral obligation supports objectivity or can instead arise from evolved concern for survival and flourishing.

lockedSections.title: Evolution and rational reliability
lockedSections.rationale: This section addresses whether an evolutionary explanation undermines confidence in reasoning itself and therefore defeats the con route.

lockedSections.title: Intuition and explanatory burden
lockedSections.rationale: This section compares the epistemic force of basic moral convictions with the narrower evolutionary project of explaining moral experience.

lockedSections.title: Ambiguity and objective morality
lockedSections.rationale: This section tests whether disagreement and ambiguous cases undermine objectivity or instead fit an evolutionary pattern centered on harm and survival.

lockedSections.title: Competing grounds of reason
lockedSections.rationale: This section contains the final direct exchange over whether evolution or theism better grounds trustworthy reason and whether the theistic answer is circular.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: Because evil is a privation of objective good and objective good is grounded in God's nature, the existence of evil supports rather than disproves God.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: Moral wrongness is dependent on conscious valuers, and invoking a transcendent being to preserve mind-independent morality would assume the very being the moral argument seeks to establish.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: The pervasive, deeply ingrained experience of moral law is an effect that should be trusted as objective and explained by a transcendent moral cause.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: Evolution can instill survival and flourishing commitments that make derivative moral rules feel objective, without making the foundational commitment objectively good.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: If undirected evolution produces every belief for survival rather than truth, it undermines confidence in moral beliefs and in the naturalistic conclusions drawn from them.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: Reason must be treated as a basic practical assumption for inquiry, and evolved consciousness can explain rational capacity even if ultimate certainty about its reliability is unavailable.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: Immediate moral obligation is a properly basic belief whose epistemic force exceeds the weaker skeptical premises used to deny objective morality.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: The evolutionary case explains why people experience actions as right or wrong; it does not claim that science makes those actions objectively right or wrong.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: Evolutionary origins threaten the reliability of all beliefs, while disagreement or uncertainty about particular moral cases no more disproves moral objectivity than scientific disagreement disproves an objective world.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: Moral ambiguity does not itself prove subjectivity, but its concentration around disputed harm, life, and survival classifications supports an evolutionary explanation of moral experience.

lockedMoves.speaker: Frank Turek
lockedMoves.proposition: If evolution gives rise to every belief, including belief in evolution, those beliefs lack a trustworthy ground unless rational capacities are designed by a rational divine mind.

lockedMoves.speaker: Alex O'Connor
lockedMoves.proposition: The theistic account faces a parallel circularity because it uses reason allegedly supplied by God to infer that God is the rational source that validates reason.
